questions.prompt: A database management system (DBMS) is:
choices: Software that stores data once and lets many programs and people query it
questions.explain: A DBMS stores the data and controls who can read and change it.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a database management system?
questions.explain: GeoTIFF is a raster file format. The others are DBMSs.

questions.prompt: PostGIS is:
choices: An extension that adds spatial types and functions to PostgreSQL
questions.explain: PostGIS turns PostgreSQL into a spatial database.

questions.prompt: A GeoPackage is built on which database?
questions.explain: A GeoPackage is a SQLite database laid out to an OGC standard.

questions.prompt: In a DBMS, users change data:
choices: Only through the DBMS, which checks their permissions
By editing the files on disk directly
questions.explain: No direct write access: the DBMS stands between users and the stored data.

questions.prompt: Concurrency in a DBMS means:
choices: Many users can read and edit at the same time
Data is stored in several copies
Every user has a private copy
questions.explain: The DBMS keeps simultaneous edits from overwriting each other.

questions.prompt: Put the three tiers of a database system in order, from the user down.
questions.explain: The client talks to the application tier, which talks to the database.

questions.prompt: A relational database:
choices: Stores data in tables linked by fields with shared values
questions.explain: Tables are related through key fields.

questions.prompt: A primary key is a field whose values:
choices: Identify each row uniquely, with no repeats
questions.explain: Forest_ID is the primary key of the Forests table.

questions.prompt: A foreign key is:
choices: A field in one table that holds values of another table's primary key
The first field of every table
A field that must be unique
questions.explain: Forest_ID in the Trails table points back to the Forests table.

questions.prompt: Values in a foreign key field can repeat.
questions.explain: Many trails can share the same Forest_ID.

questions.prompt: For a join to work, the two key fields must have the same name.
questions.explain: Name in People matched Owner in Cars. The values and types must match, not the names.

questions.prompt: For a join to work, the two key fields should have the same data type.
questions.explain: Text to text, integer to integer. A text key never matches a number key.

questions.prompt: Which makes the best key for U.S. counties?
questions.explain: Names repeat (about 30 states have a Washington County) and are spelled different ways. Codes don't.

questions.prompt: In a table join, the destination table is the one that:
choices: Receives the new fields and keeps all its rows
questions.explain: In GIS the destination is usually the layer with the geometry.

questions.prompt: In a table join, the source table:
choices: Supplies the fields that are appended
questions.explain: ArcGIS also calls it the join table.

questions.prompt: A join only works if both tables are sorted in the same order.
questions.explain: A join matches on key values, not on row positions.

questions.prompt: In QGIS and ArcGIS Pro, a join is temporary until you export the layer.
questions.explain: The join is a live link. Export to keep the fields.

questions.prompt: A collection that can contain duplicates is called a:
questions.explain: Tables are bags unless a primary key forbids repeated rows.

questions.prompt: An inner join keeps:
choices: Only rows that match in both tables
Every row of the left table
Every row of the right table
questions.explain: Unmatched rows on either side are dropped.

questions.prompt: A left join keeps:
choices: Every row of the left (destination) table, with NULL where nothing matched
Every row of the right table
questions.explain: This is the default join in QGIS and ArcGIS Pro.

questions.prompt: A full outer join keeps:
questions.explain: Unmatched rows from both sides are kept, with NULLs.

questions.prompt: STUDENT has Zhang, Shankar, Parr, and McKeon. TAKES has two enrollments for Zhang, one for Shankar, and one for a student not in STUDENT. How many rows does the inner join return?
questions.explain: Zhang's two enrollments and Shankar's one.

questions.prompt: Using the same STUDENT and TAKES tables, how many rows does the left join of STUDENT to TAKES return?
questions.explain: Zhang twice, Shankar once, and Parr and McKeon once each with NULL courses.

questions.prompt: In the People and Cars left join, Lola owns no car. Her row:
choices: Is kept, with NULL in the Car and Year fields
questions.explain: A left join keeps every destination row.

questions.prompt: In ArcGIS Pro's Add Join tool, how do you get an inner join?
questions.explain: Keep All Target Features is the left-join setting.

questions.prompt: In QGIS's Join Attributes by Field Value tool, how do you get an inner join?
choices: Check Discard records which could not be joined
questions.explain: That option drops destination records with no match.

questions.prompt: Cardinality describes:
choices: How many records in one table match each record in the other
The data type of a key
questions.explain: One-to-one, many-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many.

questions.prompt: Joining counties (destination) to states (source) is:
questions.explain: Many counties share a state; each county is in one state.

questions.prompt: Joining states (destination) to counties (source) is:
questions.explain: Each state matches many counties.

questions.prompt: Students and classes are related:
questions.explain: Each student takes many classes, and each class has many students.

questions.prompt: Which cardinalities can be joined directly, with one value per field per feature?
questions.explain: Each destination record finds at most one match.

questions.prompt: In a one-to-many join through the Joins tab, QGIS:
choices: Copies the first match and ignores the rest, with no warning
Adds every match as a new field
questions.explain: That silently drops data. Summarize the source first.

questions.prompt: You want the total county population in each state. The best approach is to:
choices: Summarize the county table by state, then join
Join the county table to the states directly
questions.explain: Summarizing gives one row per state, and the join becomes one-to-one.

questions.prompt: A relate (or relation in QGIS) differs from a join because it:
choices: Links the tables without copying fields into the layer
questions.explain: Relates handle one-to-many relationships without breaking one row per feature.

questions.prompt: A many-to-many relationship is usually handled with:
questions.explain: TAKES links STUDENT to COURSES.

questions.prompt: How many characters long is a census tract GEOID?
questions.explain: 2 for the state, 3 for the county, 6 for the tract.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of a tract GEOID in order.
questions.explain: State, then county, then tract: 37 135 010701.

questions.prompt: A census GEOID should be stored as:
questions.explain: As a number it loses its leading zeros, like California's 06.

questions.prompt: After a census join, every tract in California has NULL population. The most likely cause is:
choices: The CSV's GEOID was read as a number and lost its leading zero
The layer has too many tracts
The tracts are in a projected CRS
questions.explain: 06001400100 became 6001400100, which matches nothing.

questions.prompt: A .csvt file:
choices: Sets the data type of each column in a CSV
Holds the geometry of a CSV
questions.explain: For example "String","Integer".

questions.prompt: After a join, a handful of records are NULL while the rest worked. Which is a likely cause?
choices: Stray spaces or different capitalization in some keys
The key fields have different data types
The source table has no geometry
questions.explain: Trim spaces and standardize case before joining.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a census join in QGIS in order.
answer: Load the tract layer and find GEOID
Add the CSV as a delimited text table with no geometry
Join on the Joins tab, GEOID to GEOID
Open the attribute table and look for NULLs
questions.explain: Load, add, join, check, then make it permanent.

questions.prompt: Which question needs a spatial join rather than an attribute join?
choices: How many EMS calls fell in each neighborhood, when the calls have only coordinates
Attach census population to tracts by GEOID
Attach state names to counties by state FIPS code
Attach owner names to parcels by parcel ID
questions.explain: With no shared key, location has to do the matching.
